page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-2 is a general-purpose, memory-skewed virtual machine instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical Intel Xeon core operating at 2.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set support includes baseline AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. The platform provides 16.0 GB of memory, equating to a substantial 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The server includes no bundled local storage and contains zero GPUs, relying on persistent network storage for data retention.

Benchmark evaluations position the computational and data-handling throughput of the e2-highmem-2 in entry-level ranges. In stress-ng, it achieved a single-core score of 1101.98 and a multi-core score of 1451.88. Geekbench scores registered at 841 for single-core and 1028 for multi-core, reflecting the bounds of a single dual-threaded execution core. Memory tests demonstrated 12.0 GB/sec read and 10.51 GB/sec write throughput on uncached 256 MB blocks, alongside an 80.53 GB/sec cached small-block transfer rate. Operational testing yielded 1.33 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.43 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the e2-highmem-2 is its high memory-to-compute ratio against low aggregate CPU processing power. This profile provides resource and cost efficiency for applications bound by memory capacity rather than raw clock cycles or thread counts. Suitable workloads include in-memory caching systems, lightweight database servers, continuous integration tasks with heavy dependency graphs, low-throughput web serving, and small background ETL workers.
